We will begin with the top layer first (the waterproofing membrane) and work our way down to the fountain of your roof (the decking material).

Source: ©Georgia-Pacific Building Products - Youtube - DensDeck® Roof Board vs. HD ISO

4. Waterproofing Membrane: The top layer comprises a waterproofing membrane. Most common here in the Midwest region are TPO, PVC, or modified bitumen.

3. Cover Board: Creates a stable flat surface for the waterproofing membrane and protects the insulation below.

2. Insulation: Is specifically designed to keep the heat of summer and the cold of winter out, thus keeping your internal building envelope conditioned and comfortable. If multiple insulation layers are used, the boards are staggered to prevent seam stacking.

1. Decking Material: This structural base (or “deck”) of your roof can be made of either wood, metal, or concrete.

Now let’s take a closer look at each component:

What Is a Waterproofing Membrane?

This is the uppermost layer of your roof. On a new or replacement build, we typically recommend a waterproofing membrane be made of either TPO, PVC, or modified bitumen. However, based on the age of your building, typically the best plan is to keep whatever existing system you have operable for as long as feasible. The membrane is the surface material you would walk on, and provides your roof’s first line of defense against the rain, hail, strong winds, and the sun’s ultraviolet (UV) radiation. These membranes come in large rolls which can either be mechanically attached using screws and metal plates or fully adhered using glues and adhesives (in itself, a whole separate topic/decision, Fully Adhered vs Mechanically Attached). The seams of TPO or PVC membranes are heat welded using special equipment. Once completed, the sheets of TPO or PVC act like the liner of a swimming pool. They form a single, watertight barrier, protecting your building from water and the elements. If properly installed by a licensed and experienced roofing professional, all 3 materials (TPO, PVC, and modified bitumen) come with a warranty of up to 20-25 years.

What Is a Cover Board?

Cover board is typically a thin, dense board (aka substrate) that is placed over decking or insulation to provide a stable, flat surface for the top layer of waterproofing membrane, and to protect the softer insulation below. The cover board layer is sandwiched between the waterproof membrane and the insulation layer. While many quality options exist on the market, our team at Rhoden Roofing typically recommends one of two reliable cover board options to our low-slope commercial roofing clients: high-density (HD) Poly ISO board and DensDeck® which is a mat-faced gypsum fiber board. Cover board can either be glued down using adhesives, or it can be mechanically attached using screws and metal plates.

What Is a Roofing Insulation?

There are myriad insulation options available on the market. Here, we will focus on the 2 types of insulation that we typically recommend for our commercial customers: EPS and polyiso foam core insulation boards. EPS is a rigid, closed-cell foam insulation material made from expanded polystyrene. EPS is familiar to most of us as the lightweight styrene blocks used in packaging. EPS is manufactured in a wide variety of shapes, sizes, thicknesses, and densities for the roofing industry. Polyiso foam core insulation boards are made from closed-cell, rigid polyisocyanurate foam core and are usually bonded on both sides to facers typically made of foil or matted fiberglass. Both EPS and Poly ISO foam core boards are available in flat and tapered versions. The tapered versions are extremely helpful when flat commercial roofs do not have enough slope to drain property. The addition of a tapered insulation system by an experienced and qualified roofing professional can usually completely take care of drainage issues and eliminate standing water and ponding on your flat commercial roof. For a deeper dive, you can read more at Polyiso vs EPS Insulation and What Do I Need to Know About Tapered Insulation Panels?

What Is a Roof Decking?

No, not the place where you grill, gather, and relax on the weekends. Roof decking can be thought of as the foundation of your roof. It’s the material that is laid on top of the building’s structural members and creates a stable platform for all other roofing materials. A solid, well-installed decking layer creates stability for everything layered on top of it. There are various options for decking material, including wood-based decking (plywood and OSB), metal decking (usually corrugated and galvanized), or concrete (mixed with lightweight aggregates). Each type of decking comes with its own unique advantages and disadvantages.

How Are These 4 Components Typically Assembled?

This is just as relevant to know for a repair as a new install. Waterproofing membrane is on the top layer, then the cover board, then the insulation boards, and finally the decking material on the bottom. On the metal roof in the photo above, we are using 2 two-inch poly ISO foam core insulation boards, with a thin cover board staggered on top. Note that the seams on both of the two layers of insulation boards and the cover board are staggered. This ensures that no two seams are positioned on top of one another. This staggering technique reduces the flow of water and air between the boards in the event of water or wind intrusion, making the whole roofing system tighter and more energy-efficient.

Are There Some Roofing Systems That Do Not Have All 4 Components?

Yes, there are exceptions to this general rule. Not all roofing solutions have these components in the same order. Flute fill retrofit solutions have 2 to 3 layers of insulation, while fleeceback TPO and fleeceback PVC solutions have no cover boards under the fleeceback TPO or PVC membrane layer. We will not go into great detail here. To learn more about these exceptions please explore the links provided. If you have specific questions about your commercial flat or low slope roof, we are always here to help. Contact Rhoden Roofing for a free consultation and review of your unique roofing needs.

Summary and Key Takeaways:

  • The Layers: The 4 main components of a typical roofing system are the waterproofing membrane on top, then the cover board layer, then the insulation boards, and finally, the roof decking on the bottom.
  • Waterproofing Membrane: The top layer comprises a waterproof membrane, such as TPO, PVC, or modified bitumen. This membrane creates a uniform barrier against debris, water, wind, hail, and solar radiation.
  • Cover Board: The cover board layer creates a smooth, flat surface for the waterproofing membrane and protects the insulation below.
  • Insulation Boards: The insulation boards typically use trapped air to keep out the extreme heat of summer and the bitter cold of winter, thereby keeping your air-conditioned or heated spaces comfortable. If multiple insulation layers are used, the boards are staggered to prevent seam stacking.
  • Decking Material: This foundation of your roof can be made of either wood, metal, or concrete.
  • Exceptions to the Rule: Not all roofs are created alike and there are several exceptions to this general rule. Always feel free to call Rhoden Roofing and we will be happy to answer any questions you might have about your unique roofing needs.

title.rendered: What To Know About Natural Slate Roof Installation In Wichita

content.rendered:
If you’re considering a natural slate roof for your home, you’re likely drawn to its timeless beauty, durability, and ability to elevate the value of your property. But before committing to this premium roofing material, it’s essential to understand the unique challenges and nuances involved. This guide will walk you through the special considerations for natural slate roof installation, offering practical insights and actionable advice. Let’s explore what you need to know to make an informed decision and how Rhoden Roofing LLC can help ensure a flawless installation.

Why Choose a Natural Slate Roof

A natural slate roof offers an unmatched combination of beauty and durability. Its elegant appearance adds a refined touch to any property, while its lifespan can exceed 100 years with proper installation and maintenance. Slate is also an eco-friendly choice. It is a natural material that doesn’t rely on chemical processing, making it a great option for those looking to reduce their carbon footprint.

Beyond aesthetics and environmental benefits, slate provides exceptional insulation, helping to maintain comfortable indoor temperatures and reduce energy costs. This advantage, paired with its resistance to fire, mold, and insects, makes it one of the most reliable and long-lasting roofing options available.

Challenges Homeowners Face with Natural Slate Roofs

While the benefits of slate are undeniable, homeowners often encounter several challenges when considering this roofing option.

One common concern is the high initial investment. Natural slate can be significantly more expensive than other roofing materials, both in terms of material costs and installation. Additionally, slate’s weight requires a strong roof structure, which may necessitate reinforcement or additional support. This is often a hidden cost that homeowners don’t initially consider.

Specialized installation is another factor since improper handling can compromise the longevity and performance of the roof. Slate tiles are brittle and prone to cracking if mishandled, making it crucial to hire skilled professionals. Lastly, while slate is exceptionally durable, repairs require expertise to avoid further damage to surrounding tiles.

Understanding these challenges is key to a successful installation. Let’s break down these considerations further.

Special Considerations for Natural Slate Roof

Structural Integrity of Your Home

One of the most important aspects of a natural slate roof installation is ensuring that your home can support its weight. Slate tiles are significantly heavier than asphalt shingles or metal roofing. For this reason, a professional assessment of your roof’s structure is critical.

This is especially important for older homes, which may not have been built with slate roofing in mind. Reinforcing your roof’s framework might involve adding beams, strengthening trusses, or making other structural adjustments to handle the additional load.

At Rhoden Roofing LLC, our team conducts thorough inspections to evaluate your home’s framework. If reinforcement is needed, we provide detailed solutions to prepare your structure for a slate roof.

Choosing the Right Slate for Your Home

Not all slate is created equal. It varies in terms of thickness, color, and durability. Certain types of slate may be better suited to the climate in Wichita, where hailstorms and high winds can be a concern.

Key factors to consider include thickness, color, and weather resistance. Thicker tiles offer greater durability but add more weight, so they may not be suitable for all homes. Slate comes in a range of shades, from classic gray to vibrant greens and reds, though some colors may fade over time. Weather resistance is especially important in hail-prone areas, as certain types of slate have better impact ratings.

Rhoden Roofing LLC sources premium slate materials tailored to Wichita’s climate. Our experts guide you in selecting tiles that balance aesthetics with durability, ensuring your roof not only looks stunning but also withstands the region’s challenging weather conditions.

Expert Installation Matters

Installing a natural slate roof requires specialized skills. Unlike other roofing materials, slate cannot be nailed or cut haphazardly. Each tile must be meticulously positioned and secured to prevent breakage or water infiltration.

Common installation mistakes include using improper fasteners that corrode over time, misaligning tiles, or cutting corners on flashing and underlayment. These errors can result in leaks or uneven weight distribution.

It’s also worth noting that slate roofs are time-intensive to install. While the process may take longer than standard roofing materials, the result is a roof that lasts for generations. Rushing the installation can lead to costly problems later.

As a Crown Roofer with Ludowici and a MasterPiece Contractor with DaVinci Roofscapes, Rhoden Roofing LLC brings decades of expertise to every slate installation. Our team follows industry best practices to ensure a seamless and long-lasting result.

Maintenance and Repairs

Although durable, slate roofs are not entirely maintenance-free. Over time, individual tiles may crack or become dislodged, especially in severe weather. Attempting DIY repairs can often cause more harm than good, as slate is easily damaged without proper handling.

Regular inspections are essential to identify loose or damaged tiles before they lead to leaks or structural issues. Cleaning gutters frequently prevents water buildup, which can accelerate wear. Additionally, snow guards may be necessary in areas prone to heavy snowfall to prevent damage from sliding snow and ice.

Rhoden Roofing LLC offers professional repair services for slate roofs, ensuring any damage is addressed promptly and correctly. With our help, your roof will maintain its integrity for decades.

What to Know About Natural Slate Roof Installation in Wichita

Living in Wichita comes with unique weather challenges, including hailstorms and high winds. These factors make it essential to choose the right slate and partner with experienced professionals for the installation.

Local climate considerations include hail resistance, wind performance, and thermal performance. Selecting impact-resistant slate helps withstand hailstorms, while proper fastening techniques prevent wind damage. Slate also offers excellent insulation, keeping your home comfortable year-round and reducing energy costs during both hot summers and cold winters.

Additionally, Wichita homeowners should factor in the potential for storm damage when selecting a roofing contractor. A skilled team with local experience can anticipate these challenges and implement solutions to protect your roof long-term.

Why Rhoden Roofing LLC is the Right Choice for Your Slate Roof

At Rhoden Roofing LLC, we understand that investing in a slate roof is a significant decision. That’s why we offer unparalleled expertise, premium materials, and a commitment to customer satisfaction. From structural assessments to material selection and expert installation, we handle every step of the process.

Our lifetime workmanship warranty provides peace of mind, knowing your investment is protected. Unlike other contractors who offer limited warranties, we stand behind our work for the lifetime of your roof.

Our dedication to quality has earned us multiple awards, including the Angie’s List Super Service Award and recognition as a GAF Master Elite Contractor. We also understand the specific needs of homes in Wichita and provide customized solutions that enhance durability and performance.

Rhoden Roofing LLC is committed to making the installation process as seamless as possible. We prioritize clear communication, ensure timely project completion, and always use the highest quality materials.

Cost vs. Value: Is a Slate Roof Worth It?

Many homeowners hesitate to invest in a slate roof due to its upfront cost. However, when you consider the roof’s lifespan and minimal maintenance requirements, it becomes clear that slate offers tremendous value. Unlike other roofing materials that may need replacement every 20 to 30 years, a properly installed slate roof can last over a century, effectively paying for itself over time.

Furthermore, slate’s natural beauty enhances curb appeal and increases property value, making it a wise choice for homeowners looking to maximize their investment.

Ready to Elevate Your Home with a Natural Slate Roof

A natural slate roof is more than just a functional choice—it’s an investment in your home’s beauty and longevity. By addressing the unique challenges of slate installation and partnering with experts like Rhoden Roofing LLC, you can ensure your roof performs flawlessly for generations.

For more information about special considerations for natural slate roof or to learn more about what to know about natural slate roof installation in Wichita, contact us at 316-927-2233. Let Rhoden Roofing LLC help you achieve the roof of your dreams.

When it comes to roofing, homeowners often face a variety of decisions—style, durability, cost, and more. If you’re exploring premium options, slate roofing stands out as one of the most timeless and reliable materials available. But is it the right choice for your home in Wichita? Let’s dive into the reasons to choose a slate roof and how it can benefit your property in ways that other materials cannot.

Why Homeowners Consider Slate Roofing

As a homeowner, you likely want a roof that combines beauty, longevity, and durability. But with so many roofing materials available, making the right choice can feel overwhelming. While asphalt shingles may be popular for their affordability, they often lack the high-end appeal and lifespan that some homeowners desire.

Slate roofing addresses these concerns with a combination of aesthetic appeal and lasting value. Below, we’ll explore the advantages of slate roofing to help you make an informed decision.

Unmatched Longevity

Slate roofs are known for their exceptional lifespan, often lasting 75-100 years or more with proper care. Unlike other materials that may require frequent repairs or replacement, a slate roof offers long-term peace of mind.

Why Longevity Matters

Reduced costs over time are a significant benefit of slate roofing. While the upfront investment in slate is higher, the durability often eliminates the need for a second roof in your lifetime. Additionally, choosing a material with such a long lifespan means less waste in landfills compared to shorter-lived roofing options.

At Rhoden Roofing LLC, we specialize in the expert installation of slate roofs, ensuring you maximize this impressive longevity with precision craftsmanship.

Timeless Beauty and Curb Appeal

One of the key reasons to choose a slate roof is its unparalleled aesthetic appeal. Available in a variety of colors, textures, and patterns, slate roofs complement virtually any architectural style, from historic homes to modern builds.

Customization Options

Slate roofing offers a range of choices. You can select from shades like gray, green, black, and even red to match your home’s style. Additionally, smooth or rough finishes provide flexibility in achieving the look you desire.

A slate roof installed by Rhoden Roofing will not only protect your home but also make it a standout in your neighborhood.

Superior Durability

In areas like Wichita, where hail and strong winds can take a toll on roofs, durability is a critical factor. Slate is one of the strongest roofing materials available, capable of resisting hail impact, high winds, and even fire.

Long-Term Protection

Thanks to its natural stone composition, slate is far less prone to damage than asphalt shingles or even some metal roofs. This means fewer repairs and more reliable protection for your home.

Rhoden Roofing offers expert advice and installation services to ensure your slate roof is ready to tackle Wichita’s unpredictable weather.

Low Maintenance

Many roofing materials require ongoing maintenance to prevent issues like leaks or rot. Slate roofing, on the other hand, demands minimal upkeep due to its durable and water-resistant properties.

Key Benefits of Low Maintenance

Natural stone resists common issues like warping or mold growth, which results in fewer repairs over the years. Additionally, with less maintenance required, you’ll save on long-term repair costs.

Our team at Rhoden Roofing ensures every slate roof installation is done with precision, minimizing the chances of future maintenance headaches.

Environmentally Friendly

For homeowners looking to reduce their environmental impact, slate roofing is a top contender. Its natural composition and long lifespan make it an eco-friendly choice.

Sustainability Features

Slate is quarried from the earth, avoiding the need for synthetic materials. At the end of its life, slate can be reused or recycled rather than sent to a landfill.

Choosing a slate roof with Rhoden Roofing not only protects your home but also supports a more sustainable future.

Why Choose Rhoden Roofing for Your Slate Roof?

While the advantages of slate roofing are clear, its successful installation requires expertise. Slate is heavier and more delicate than other roofing materials, meaning improper installation can lead to costly problems.

Certified Expertise

As a Ludowici Crown Roofer and DaVinci Roofscapes Masterpiece Contractor, we have the skills and certifications to handle slate roof installations with care and precision.

Attention to Detail

From selecting the right slate tiles to ensuring proper structural support, we leave no detail overlooked.

Long-Term Support

With our Lifetime Workmanship Warranty, you can rest assured that we stand behind every roof we install.

Is a Slate Roof Right for You?

While slate roofing offers numerous benefits, it’s important to consider factors like cost and weight. Slate is a premium material, so its upfront cost is higher than asphalt or metal. Additionally, the structure of your home must be strong enough to support its weight.

Not sure if slate is the right fit? Rhoden Roofing is here to guide you. Our team will evaluate your home, discuss your goals, and provide personalized recommendations to meet your needs and budget.

Ready to Upgrade to Slate?

Choosing the right roof is about more than just protecting your home—it’s about investing in beauty, durability, and peace of mind. The advantages of slate roofing make it an exceptional choice for homeowners in Wichita who want a roof that truly stands the test of time.

Call Rhoden Roofing LLC at 316-927-2233 today to schedule a consultation and explore the reasons to choose a slate roof for your home. Our team is ready to bring your vision to life with expert installation and unmatched customer service.

title.rendered: A Homeowners Guide to Clay Tile Roofs

content.rendered:
If you’ve visited New York City, residents there note that they recognize tourists by how often they look up. Tourists aren’t used to seeing skyscrapers. In Kansas and the Midwest, people respond similarly when they see a clay tile roof. They’re uncommon, eye-catching, and a colorful departure from the asphalt shingles that protect most homes.

Clay tile roofs are commonly found in the Southwestern region of the United States where high temperatures, unimpeded by clouds or rain, are prevalent. In the lower Midwest, clay tile roofs are rare – rare enough that people double-take or glance a second longer when they see one on a historic or commercial property.

For homeowners, clay tile offers visual appeal and longevity. With proper maintenance, these roofs can last a century. In this guide, we’ll cover how to care for them, how they influence insurance premiums and other costs, and how they compare to standard roof systems. If you’re considering installing a clay tile roof, you’ll gain a clear sense of whether this roof material that’s both uncommon in Kansas and striking is the right fit for your home.

Owners of historic buildings often choose clay tile for its timeless appearance. It complements heritage architecture with an authentic appearance while requiring minimal maintenance. For restorations like this historic train depot, clay tile both preserves the building’s original aesthetic and provides more modern durability. 

 

Why Consider a Clay Tile Roof

Clay tile roofs are an excellent choice for homeowners seeking a blend of beauty and resilience. They offer unmatched performance and visual appeal, making them ideal for various home styles and climates. But why consider a clay tile roof? Let’s dive into its unique features and how they compare to other roof materials. 

Factor Clay Tile Concrete Tile Asphalt Shingles
Durability 50–100 years; centuries in warm, dry climates. 40–75 years; nearly as durable as clay, but more vulnerable to cracking, especially with foot traffic. 15–25 years; shortest lifespan of the three.
Upfront Cost High; among the most expensive roofing materials per square foot. Medium-high; up to 20–30% less expensive than clay. Low; cheapest option up front, though more frequent replacements add up.**
Energy Efficiency* Excellent (W/mK = 0.840); high natural thermal density reduces attic temperature, and S-shaped or barrel tile design provides breathability. Good (W/mK = 1.10); higher conductivity than clay but still good. High thermal density but less effective at slowing heat transfer. Low; no thermal density, but surface temperature can exceed 160 °F on a hot summer day.
Structural Needs Heavy; often requires reinforced decking and structural framing. Heavy; similar weight loads to clay. Light; ~4,200 pounds per 10 squares, which is less than half the weight of tile. No reinforcement needed.
Maintenance Frequency Low; tile replacement is necessary only if one cracks or breaks. Low-Medium; slightly more prone to surface cracks than clay tiles. High; shingles lose granules and wear over time.
Property Value Impact High; boosts curb appeal and resale value. Moderate; durable and often visually appealing but lacks the prestige of clay. Neutral; standard asphalt shingles rarely increase property value beyond the value of basic protection.

*Note 1: λ, or W/mK, represents thermal conductivity. This is the rate at which heat can move through a material. Clay’s lower λ suggests that it is best at delaying heat entry into the attic – one of the reasons it is prevalent in sun-soaked regions, although exact values may vary depending on the product’s density and firing process.

**Note 2: An asphalt shingle roof will require two or three total replacements over the course of 60 years. A well-maintained clay or concrete tile roof is unlikely to require a single replacement in a 60-year span.

 

Longevity That Outlasts Other Materials

Clay tiles are built to last. Unlike asphalt shingles, which may require replacement every 15-25 years, clay tile roofs often have a lifespan of 50-100 years. This remarkable longevity makes them an investment for homeowners planning to stay in their homes long-term. The key to its durability is its kiln-fired manufacturing process.

Clay is naturally porous and soft, no different than dirt. If you’ve walked through wet clay, you’ve seen how it clumps and sticks. This is a glimpse into the binding qualities that make clay so versatile: when it’s shaped into tiles and fired in a kiln at temperatures exceeding 2,000°F, the heat vitrifies the clay particles, filling its natural pores and creating a dense, hardened surface.

Eco-Friendly and Sustainable

Clay tiles are made from natural materials, making them an environmentally friendly roofing option. They’re recyclable and require minimal processing, reducing their environmental impact compared to synthetic materials.

Consider the contrast with asphalt shingles. Asphalt is derived from bitumen, a heavy byproduct of refining oil. It’s like butter and buttermilk: butter is the product people want, buttermilk is the leftover product that has a few uses. In this case, the asphalt in asphalt shingles is the buttermilk of the petroleum industry.

Clay, by comparison, began its life long before industrial byproducts existed. Its existence as a roofing material results from a simple process: add water, mold it, fire it, and let it harden. This process doesn’t produce waste or byproducts. When a clay tile roof reaches the end of its service life, the tiles can be repurposed whole or recycled into new tiles.

Long-Lasting Visual Appeal

Clay tiles have been used to protect buildings for centuries. Ancient Rome’s terracotta roofs and the Spanish missions in the southwestern United States, both over a thousand years and miles apart, use clay tiles. Its bright color that’s naturally infused into the material is the primary aesthetic appeal of clay tiles today, but two features contribute to their aesthetic appeal: shape and texture.

  • Shape: Clay tiles have myriad profiles, from barrel-shaped tiles to flat, modern cuts. This allows them to enhance different architectural styles and provide a silhouette for any property. A Spanish villa, a stucco-clad commercial property, or a modern minimalist home can equally benefit from clay tile.
  • Texture: Because clay is soft and moldable before entering the kiln, textures can be applied to tiles. They range from rugged and rustic finishes (e.g., Ludowici’s “Weathered” texture) to smooth and refined (e.g., Ludowici’s “Smooth” texture). Similar to high profile hip and ridge caps on an asphalt shingle roof, these options can provide depth and allow homeowners to match their home’s character, whether it’s weathered and authentic or clean and contemporary.

 

A clay tile roof that required a lift and relay 20 years after its installation. Water damming started to occur at the battens, which required a more modern elevated batten system to resolve. Underlayment was replaced and original tiles were harvested from back slopes to replace damaged tiles at the front of the house. New tiles were placed where original tiles were harvested from. Despite a few cracked tiles, the original shingles were in excellent shape. 

Benefits of Clay Tile Roofs

Understanding the benefits of clay tile roofs can help you decide whether they’re the right fit for your home. Here’s why they’ve been a trusted choice for centuries.

Durability in Extreme Conditions

Clay tile roofs are incredibly durable, standing up to harsh weather conditions, including heavy rain, strong winds, and even hail. They also meet the highest fire resistance rating of Class A from UL Solutions.

The resilience of clay tile also earned it a class 4 impact-resistance rating from UL Solutions, which qualifies homes with clay tile roofs for an insurance premium discount with some insurance carriers.

For more information on what affects homeowner’s insurance premiums, read our guide outlining how roofs affect your insurance premiums.

Energy Efficiency

Clay tiles naturally insulate your home, helping regulate indoor temperatures. This can lead to reduced heating and cooling costs, making your home more energy-efficient year-round.

Asphalt shingles contain much more than asphalt. They have stone granules on top, layers of asphalt in the middle, and a fiberglass mat at the bottom.

Clay tile roofs are aptly named: they are made with molded clay that’s heated in a kiln. Clay provides exceptional thermal density, meaning it heats up slowly and cools down quickly.

Clay tiles are commonly molded into an S-shape or U shape for barrel tiles. Combined with battens, narrow wood strips installed over the underlayment, clay tiles allow for airflow without allowing water to infiltrate – one of the reasons clay tiles require a 5:12 minimum slope. Air circulation in elevated batten systems can significantly reduce roof temperatures.

Low Maintenance

With proper installation and occasional maintenance, clay tile roofs require minimal upkeep. Unlike other materials that deteriorate over time, clay tiles retain their strength and appearance for decades.

Clay tiles don’t fade in appearance as they age. Instead, they may develop a patina, a natural color change in the material that can further enhance their appearance without compromising their integrity.

All maintenance should be performed by a qualified, experienced contractor. Avoid walking on the tiles unless necessary, and only step where tiles overlap at the bottom.

Increased Property Value

A clay tile roof is seen as a long-term investment by both the homeowner installing it and potential home buyers. It’s associated with durability, energy efficiency, and curb appeal, all of which can increase the home’s value when it’s time to sell.

Some clay tile roof manufacturer warranties that extend to 75 years and can be transferred to the next homeowner, which is attractive to prospective buyers.

Key Considerations Before Installing Clay Tile

Clay tile roofs are beautiful and durable, but they aren’t the right fit for every home. Their added weight, installation demands, and higher initial cost mean they come with additional considerations. This doesn’t take away from their strengths. It just means that clay tile roofs require planning, expertise, and occasional structural adjustments. Below we walk through the most common concerns we hear from homeowners, as well as how they’re addressed in practice.

Structural Considerations

Clay tiles are heavier than other roofing materials, and your home’s structure must support the additional weight. Our team conducts thorough structural assessments and, if necessary, provides reinforcement recommendations to ensure your home is ready for a clay tile roof.

1,000 square feet (or 10 squares) of architectural asphalt shingles weigh approximately 4,200 pounds.
1,000 square feet of clay Spanish barrel tiles can weigh closer to 10,000 pounds.

Put another way, switching from asphalt to clay is like replacing a pickup truck with a fully loaded semi on your roof. Even if the ceiling doesn’t collapse, failing to properly reinforce the structure if needed can cause the framing of the house to bow under the load.

Installation Expertise

Installing a clay tile roof requires specialized skills. Our certified technicians have extensive experience with clay tile installation, ensuring precise placement and sealing techniques to maximize your roof’s performance and longevity.

Upfront Costs

Clay tile roofs often have the highest upfront cost of any sloped roof material. For more information, see our related guide on roof replacement costs. Clay tile has a few special considerations, however:

  • Increased Labor Cost: Clay tiles demand careful handling. Tiles must be carefully loaded onto the roof, often with a telehandler, and then placed one by one. Due to their weight and fragility when mishandled, clay tiles can’t be bundled and carried up ladders. Installers navigate the roof carefully and with precision to avoid risking damage to any installed tiles.
  • Structural Reinforcement (if needed): If a home was not originally designed for a heavy clay or concrete tile roof, it will likely require structural reinforcement to support the additional weight. Depending on your home’s condition and design, installing supports or upgrading trusses may cost between $1,000 and $10,000.
  • Premium Metals: Installation quality can influence future maintenance. If standard fasteners and galvanized flashing are used, they are likely to corrode and fail before the tile itself, potentially causing a premature lift-and-relay. One metal is the exception: copper. Copper fasteners and flashing are resistant to corrosion and can rival clay tile’s service life. This raises upfront costs but decreases the likelihood of future leaks and repairs. Copper fasteners paired with copper flashing will decrease the likelihood that a clay tile roof will require a premature lift and relay, or replacement of the underlying roof materials. They will increase the installation cost but decrease 1) the likelihood of leak-related issues, and 2) future expenses.

  • Regions without a qualified contractor make the effective installation of a clay tile roof risky. They are remarkably resilient to impact forces from hail, but sensitive to improper handling and tensile forces. Handling clay tiles before, during, and after installation requires care and experience. Crab crawling up the roof may appear undignified, but its even distribution of weight can reduce the risk of causing damage.

Proper care is essential to protect your clay tile roof and maximize its lifespan. Here’s how you can keep your roof in top condition.

Regular Inspections

Schedule professional inspections at least once a year to identify and address any damage early. Look for cracked or displaced tiles, which can lead to water infiltration if not repaired promptly.

Cleaning and Debris Removal

We generally recommend a one percent bleach solution or a simple low-pressure wash followed by sweeping with a soft-bristled brush.

This roof was previously natural wood shake. When the wood shake’s service life was up, the homeowner switched to Brava’s synthetic clay tiles that captured the character of natural clay without the need for structural reinforcement. 

New clay tiles installed on a historic building. 

Clay Tile vs. Synthetic Tile

Clay tiles are timeless; Brava’s synthetic tiles are timely. They look nearly identical from the ground, but with three key differences for homeowners.

  • Reduced Weight: While material costs between clay tiles and synthetic tiles are comparable, synthetic tiles are significantly lighter. Brava’s synthetic Spanish tiles weigh approximately 281 pounds per square, while architectural asphalt shingles weigh approximately 400 pounds per square. This eliminates the need for structural reinforcement and can reduce transportation and labor costs.
  • Improved Tensile Strength: The polymers that synthetic tiles are made with allow it to lightly flex and recover. This reduces the need to crab walk up a roof to evenly distribute pressure, although synthetic tiles have minimal surface friction.
  • Less Maintenance: Clay tiles are liable to chip and crack over time after. Synthetic tiles flex under pressure and are not porous, meaning they are less likely to suffer freeze-thaw damage or algal growth.

Longevity and Warranties

An important similarity between clay and synthetic tile is their durability, as we discussed in this article. Both can have serviceable lifespans of 50 years. Because these materials are likely to outlast other parts of the roof system, it’s important for homeowners to consider both material and workmanship warranties.

  • Material Warranties: These are offered by the manufacturer and typically cover defects in the product on the roof itself.
  • Workmanship Warranties: These are offered by the contractor and cover the roof’s installation.

Ideally, homeowners use a contractor whose workmanship warranty period aligns with the product’s expected service life. Tile roofs, especially barrel or S-shaped tiles, rely heavily on quality underlayment and flashings to mitigate water intrusion. As a result, workmanship errors at those layers, or the use of low-quality fasteners or flashings, don’t always cause leaks right away. They only surface during wind-driven rain or as the underlayment ages. For clay or synthetic tile roofs, the underlayment will age much earlier than the shingles.

To learn what to look for in a workmanship warranty, check out our overview here.

If you’ve visited New York City, residents there note that they recognize tourists by how often they look up. Tourists aren’t used to seeing skyscrapers. In Kansas and the Midwest, people respond similarly when they see a clay tile roof. They’re uncommon, eye-catching, and a colorful departure from the asphalt shingles that protect most homes.

Clay tile roofs are commonly found in the Southwestern region of the United States where high temperatures, unimpeded by clouds or rain, are prevalent. In the lower Midwest, clay tile roofs are rare – rare enough that people double-take or glance a second longer when they see one on a historic or commercial property.

For homeowners, clay tile offers visual appeal and longevity. With proper maintenance, these roofs can last a century. In this guide, we’ll cover how to care for them, how they influence insurance premiums and other costs, and how they compare to standard roof systems. If you’re considering installing a clay tile roof, you’ll gain a clear sense of whether this roof material that’s both uncommon in Kansas and striking is the right fit for your home.

Why Consider a Clay Tile Roof

Clay tile roofs are an excellent choice for homeowners seeking a blend of beauty and resilience. They offer unmatched performance and visual appeal, making them ideal for various home styles and climates. But why consider a clay tile roof? Let’s dive into its unique features and how they compare to other roof materials.

High thermal density but less effective at slowing heat transfer.Low; no thermal density, but surface temperature can exceed 160 °F on a hot summer day.
Structural NeedsHeavy; often requires reinforced decking and structural framing.Heavy; similar weight loads to clay.Light; ~4,200 pounds per 10 squares, which is less than half the weight of tile. No reinforcement needed.
Maintenance FrequencyLow; tile replacement is necessary only if one cracks or breaks.Low-Medium; slightly more prone to surface cracks than clay tiles.High; shingles lose granules and wear over time.

*Note 1: λ, or W/mK, represents thermal conductivity. This is the rate at which heat can move through a material. Clay’s lower λ suggests that it is best at delaying heat entry into the attic – one of the reasons it is prevalent in sun-soaked regions, although exact values may vary depending on the product’s density and firing process.

**Note 2: An asphalt shingle roof will require two or three total replacements over the course of 60 years. A well-maintained clay or concrete tile roof is unlikely to require a single replacement in a 60-year span.

Longevity That Outlasts Other Materials

Clay tiles are built to last. Unlike asphalt shingles, which may require replacement every 15-25 years, clay tile roofs often have a lifespan of 50-100 years. This remarkable longevity makes them an investment for homeowners planning to stay in their homes long-term. The key to its durability is its kiln-fired manufacturing process.

Clay is naturally porous and soft, no different than dirt. If you’ve walked through wet clay, you’ve seen how it clumps and sticks. This is a glimpse into the binding qualities that make clay so versatile: when it’s shaped into tiles and fired in a kiln at temperatures exceeding 2,000°F, the heat vitrifies the clay particles, filling its natural pores and creating a dense, hardened surface.

Clay tiles are made from natural materials, making them an environmentally friendly roofing option. They’re recyclable and require minimal processing, reducing their environmental impact compared to synthetic materials.

It’s like butter and buttermilk: butter is the product people want, buttermilk is the leftover product that has a few uses. In this case, the asphalt in asphalt shingles is the buttermilk of the petroleum industry.

Clay, by comparison, began its life long before industrial byproducts existed. Its existence as a roofing material results from a simple process: add water, mold it, fire it, and let it harden. Asphalt shingles contain much more than asphalt. They have stone granules on top, layers of asphalt in the middle, and a fiberglass mat at the bottom.

title.rendered: How Are Synthetic Tile Roofs Made

content.rendered:
Are you exploring long-lasting and low-maintenance roofing options for your home or business? Synthetic tile roofs have gained popularity as a versatile, durable, and visually appealing alternative to traditional materials. But have you ever wondered how synthetic tile roofs are made or what makes them such a reliable choice?

At Rhoden Roofing LLC, we specialize in installing premium roofing systems, including synthetic tiles that combine innovative design with unmatched durability. Let’s delve into the production process and uncover the secrets behind their remarkable strength and longevity.

Why Choose Synthetic Tile Roofs

Traditional roofing materials like clay tiles, wood shakes, and asphalt shingles have long been popular. However, they come with challenges:

Clay tiles are heavy and prone to cracking.
Wood shakes require frequent maintenance and can deteriorate over time.
Asphalt shingles are economical but often lack long-term durability.

Synthetic tiles address these issues by offering a roofing solution that mimics the look of traditional materials while outperforming them in resilience, maintenance, and sustainability.

How Are Synthetic Tile Roofs Made

The manufacturing process for synthetic tile roofs involves a blend of advanced material science and state-of-the-art engineering. These tiles are meticulously crafted to replicate the appearance of natural materials while incorporating features that enhance durability and performance.

Raw Materials Selection

The process begins with the selection of high-quality polymers and composite materials. These materials are specifically chosen for their ability to withstand harsh environmental conditions. Key features of these materials include:

UV resistance to prevent fading from prolonged sun exposure
Impact strength to resist hail, debris, and other potential damages
Lightweight properties for easier installation and reduced structural stress

Mixing and Compounding

The raw materials are blended with stabilizers, pigments, and other additives to create a polymer compound. This mixture ensures:

Color consistency, with pigments infused directly into the material to prevent surface wear
Flexibility, reducing the risk of cracks during temperature fluctuations

Molding and Shaping

Once the compound is ready, it undergoes precision molding using advanced equipment. During this stage:

Tiles are formed into shapes that mimic clay, slate, or wood textures
Intricate surface details are added for a natural appearance
Edges are smoothed for seamless installation

Curing and Cooling

After molding, the tiles are cured to solidify their structure. Controlled cooling ensures they maintain their shape and achieve optimal strength.

Quality Control and Testing

Every batch of synthetic tiles undergoes rigorous testing to meet industry standards. Tests evaluate:

Impact resistance for hail and debris
Water resistance to ensure no absorption or leakage
Temperature performance to handle extreme heat and cold

 

 

What Makes Synthetic Tiles Durable

The durability of synthetic tiles lies in their thoughtful engineering and material composition. Here’s why they outperform traditional options:

UV and Weather Resistance

Synthetic tiles are infused with UV stabilizers, preventing sun exposure from degrading their color or structure. They are also designed to handle extreme weather conditions, including heavy rain, intense heat, and sub-zero temperatures.

Impact Strength

The flexible nature of the polymers used in synthetic tiles allows them to absorb impacts without cracking. This makes them ideal for regions prone to hailstorms or falling debris.

Lightweight Yet Strong

Unlike clay or concrete tiles, synthetic tiles are lightweight, which reduces strain on the roof’s structure while still offering exceptional strength.

Longevity with Low Maintenance

Synthetic tiles resist mold, mildew, and rot, significantly reducing the need for repairs or replacements. With proper installation, these roofs can last 50 years or more.

The Environmental Advantage of Synthetic Tiles

Synthetic tiles are not only durable but also eco-friendly. Many manufacturers incorporate recycled materials into their production process, reducing waste and promoting sustainability. Additionally, their long lifespan means fewer replacements and less material waste over time.

Why Rhoden Roofing LLC Recommends Synthetic Tile Roofs

As one of the leading roofing companies in Wichita, Rhoden Roofing LLC is proud to offer premium synthetic tile roofing solutions. Here’s why we stand by these innovative products:

Proper installation is key to unlocking the full potential of synthetic tiles. Our certified professionals are trained to handle the precise techniques required for flawless installation, ensuring a secure and lasting roof.

We work with trusted manufacturers like DaVinci Roofscapes, offering you access to products with industry-leading warranties.

Synthetic tiles mimic the beauty of natural materials like slate or wood, giving your home an upscale appearance without the maintenance headaches.

At Rhoden Roofing, we don’t just install roofs; we guarantee our work for the lifetime of your roof. If you ever experience an issue caused by installation, we’ll take care of it—no exceptions.

Cost-Effectiveness: A Long-Term Investment

While synthetic tiles may have a higher upfront cost than asphalt shingles, their longevity and durability make them a cost-effective roofing choice in the long run. Benefits include:

Lower repair and replacement costs due to their resilience
Energy efficiency, as their design often helps reduce heating and cooling expenses
Increased property value with a roof that offers lasting beauty and performance

Are Synthetic Tiles Right for Your Roof

Synthetic tile roofs are an excellent choice for homeowners and business owners seeking a balance of beauty, durability, and sustainability. However, every property is unique, and the best roofing solution depends on your specific needs and budget.

Key Questions to Consider

Is your current roof prone to damage from weather or impact?
Are you looking for a low-maintenance alternative to natural materials?
Do you want a roof that combines longevity with aesthetic appeal?

Your Next Steps with Rhoden Roofing LLC

Understanding how synthetic tile roofs are made and what makes synthetic tiles durable is just the beginning. At Rhoden Roofing LLC, we’re committed to helping you find the ideal roofing solution for your property.

Why Choose Us?

Over 13 years of industry experience
Certifications from top manufacturers, including DaVinci and Ludowici
Award-winning customer service backed by a Lifetime Workmanship Warranty

Call us today at 316-927-2233 to schedule a consultation or learn more about our synthetic tile roofing options. Let us help you install a roof that offers the perfect combination of beauty, strength, and peace of mind.

Durability and Longevity

Tile roofs are renowned for their resilience. They withstand harsh weather conditions like hail and high winds, which are common in Wichita. With proper installation and maintenance, tile roofs can last over 50 years, making them a cost-effective and long-term solution for homeowners seeking reliability and peace of mind.

Aesthetic Versatility

Tile roofs offer a range of styles, colors, and textures. Whether you prefer a Mediterranean, Spanish, or modern look, tile options can complement any architectural style. This versatility allows homeowners to achieve a personalized aesthetic that enhances the curb appeal and value of their property.

Energy Efficiency

Tile roofing systems are excellent insulators, reducing heat transfer and helping regulate indoor temperatures. By keeping your home cooler in the summer and warmer in the winter, tile roofs can lead to significant energy savings, making them an environmentally friendly and cost-effective choice.

Types of Tile Roofs: Exploring Your Options

1. Clay Tile Roofs

Clay tiles are a classic choice, known for their distinctive color and long-lasting durability.

  • Pros: Clay tiles can last over 100 years with minimal maintenance. They are fire-resistant, insect-proof, and have excellent thermal properties, making them suitable for Wichita’s climate.
  • Cons: While highly durable, clay tiles are heavy and may require additional structural support. They are also more expensive and can be prone to cracking if mishandled during installation or maintenance.

2. Concrete Tile Roofs

Concrete tiles are an affordable alternative to clay tiles, offering similar benefits.

  • Pros: These tiles are available in various colors and styles, including options that mimic other roofing materials like slate or wood. Concrete tiles are highly durable, weather-resistant, and can be reinforced for additional strength.
  • Cons: Concrete tiles are heavier than clay, requiring adequate structural support. They may also absorb more moisture, leading to color fading over time.

3. Slate Tile Roofs

Slate tiles offer a distinctive and long-lasting option, though they are less common in Wichita.

  • Pros: Slate roofs can last over 100 years and provide an elegant, natural appearance. They are fire-resistant and made from a 100% natural material, adding to their appeal.
  • Cons: Slate tiles are among the most expensive roofing options and require specialized installation. They are also very heavy, necessitating significant structural reinforcement.

Important Considerations for Tile Roofing in Wichita

When selecting a tile roof for your Wichita home, several factors should influence your decision:

1. Climate Resilience

Wichita’s climate can be challenging, with hot summers, cold winters, and the potential for severe storms. All the tile types mentioned can endure these conditions, but it’s crucial to ensure professional installation and regular maintenance to maximize their longevity and performance.

2. Architectural Style Compatibility

The style of your home should also guide your choice. Clay tiles are ideal for Mediterranean or Spanish-style designs, while concrete tiles are versatile enough to fit various architectural themes. Slate is perfect for traditional or historic homes that demand a distinctive and classic look.

3. Budget Considerations

Tile roofs come with higher upfront costs more than other roofing materials. However, their long-term durability and low maintenance requirements can make them a valuable investment over time. Consider both initial expenses and lifetime value when choosing a tile roofing system.

4. Structural Requirements

Given their weight, tile roofs may need additional support structures, especially for older homes not originally designed for such loads. Ensure that a structural assessment is conducted before installation to prevent future issues and guarantee safety.

title.rendered: How Long do Cedar Roofs Last in Wichita

content.rendered:
Wichita’s climate is as dynamic as a rollercoaster ride—hot, dry summers sizzle into crisp, chilly winters, and let’s not forget the occasional spring storm. Amidst these weather whims, homeowners often find themselves pondering the durability of their roofing. At Rhoden Roofing LLC, we know that a cedar roof isn’t just a roof; it’s a statement. Cedar roofing brings a natural, rustic charm that’s hard to beat, and we’re here to break down just how long you can expect that beauty to last.

Why Cedar Roofing?

Cedar roofs are like the artisan cheese of roofing materials—distinctive, high-quality, and oh-so-appealing. They offer a warm, timeless look that stands out from the cookie-cutter asphalt shingles you see everywhere. At Rhoden Roofing LLC, we’re passionate about installing both cedar shake and cedar shingle roofs, each with its own flair.

Cedar Shake vs. Cedar Shingle: What’s the Difference?

Cedar shakes and cedar shingles are two types of cedar roofing that offer different vibes. Cedar shakes are the more rugged, hand-split option. They’re like the rough-hewn wood furniture of roofing—textured and charmingly imperfect. Shingles, on the other hand, are machine-cut and smoother, providing a more uniform appearance. They’re the polished, sleek counterpart to shakes.

Both types have a reputation for being tough as nails, but they come with different aesthetics and benefits. Cedar shakes can add a bit of a storybook feel to your home, while cedar shingles offer a more streamlined, classic look. Both types of cedar roofing can last quite a while with the right care, which is a pretty impressive lifespan for any roofing material.

How Long Can You Expect Cedar Roofs to Last?

Cedar roofs can usually last up to 25 years in Wichita’s climate. That’s right—whether you choose the rustic charm of cedar shakes or the refined elegance of cedar shingles, you’re investing in a roof that’s built to weather the storms and sunshine alike. The longevity of your cedar roof, however, isn’t just about the material; it’s also about how well you maintain it.

Maintaining Your Cedar Roof: The Secret to Cedar Roof Longevity

To ensure your cedar roof lasts as long as possible, it’s all about regular upkeep. Here are some tips to keep your cedar roof looking fantastic and functioning well:

Regular Inspections: Twice a year, ideally in the spring and fall, get up there (or better yet, call us!) to check for damage or wear. Look for missing or damaged shakes or shingles, and address issues promptly.

Keep it Clean: It’s smart to get rid of leaves and branches that can trap a lot of moisture and lead to things like mold or rot. A gentle hose-down can help keep your roof looking clean, but avoid high-pressure washing, which can damage the wood.

Remove Moss & Algae: These can grow on cedar roofs, particularly in shaded areas. If you spot them, treat the affected areas with a specialized cleaner.

Is it Properly Ventilated? Proper attic ventilation helps prevent moisture buildup, which can prematurely deteriorate your cedar roof. 

Let Rhoden Roofing LLC Take Care of Your Cedar Roof

A cedar roof isn’t just a roofing choice; it’s a lifestyle statement that enhances the beauty and value of your home. With proper installation and maintenance, it’s a roof that can last up to 25 years, standing strong against Wichita’s diverse climate. At Rhoden Roofing LLC, we’re experts in both cedar shake and cedar shingle roofing, and we’re here to ensure your roof not only lasts but thrives.

Ready to give your home the cedar roof it deserves? Contact Rhoden Roofing LLC today for a consultation, and let’s get started on adding that unique, timeless touch to your home. Your roof—and your home—will thank you!

title.rendered: Debunking 5 Cedar Roof Myths: Clarifying Misconceptions About Cedar Roofs

content.rendered:
At Rhoden Roofing LLC, we have a wealth of experience in the roofing industry, particularly with cedar roofing. Our expertise enables us to address and debunk common cedar roof myths that often lead to confusion. Understanding the true advantages of cedar roofs and clarifying these misconceptions can help you make an informed choice for your home. Let’s set the record straight on five prevalent cedar roof myths.

Myth: Cedar Roofs Are Too Expensive Compared to Other Roofing Materials

One of the most common misconceptions about cedar roofs is that they are prohibitively expensive. While cedar roofing may have a higher upfront cost compared to asphalt shingles, it’s essential to consider the long-term benefits. The advantages of cedar roofs include their durability and longevity. Cedar shakes and shingles can last up to 25 years or more with proper maintenance, potentially leading to fewer replacements and repairs over time. Additionally, cedar roofs are known for their energy efficiency, which can reduce heating and cooling costs. In the long run, the initial investment in cedar roofing is often offset by its extended lifespan and energy-saving properties.

Myth: Cedar Roofs Require Excessive Maintenance

Another common myth is that cedar roofs require a lot of maintenance. While cedar roofs do need regular care, it’s not as daunting as some might believe. Maintenance typically involves cleaning to remove moss and mildew and inspecting the roof for potential damage. Properly treated cedar roofs are resistant to issues like rot and insect damage. With the right maintenance routine, you can keep your cedar roof in excellent condition with minimal effort. At Rhoden Roofing LLC, we provide guidance on effective maintenance practices to help you enjoy the benefits of cedar roofing without unnecessary hassle.

Myth: Cedar Roofs Are Highly Flammable

There’s a widespread misconception that cedar roofs are highly flammable and pose a significant fire risk. While cedar does have some natural flammability, modern treatments and coatings have greatly enhanced its fire resistance. Fire retardant treatments can significantly reduce the risk of ignition, and many areas with high fire risk have regulations to ensure cedar roofs are treated for safety. By working with a professional contractor who applies these treatments and adheres to local building codes, you can ensure that your cedar roof remains safe and compliant. At Rhoden Roofing LLC, we prioritize safety and adhere to stringent standards to provide reliable cedar roofing solutions.

Myth: Cedar Roofs Attract Pests

A common belief is that cedar roofs attract pests like termites and woodpeckers. However, cedar roofs are often more resistant to pests than other materials. Cedar wood contains natural oils that repel insects, making it less appealing to pests like termites. Although no roofing material is completely immune to pests, proper installation and maintenance can minimize potential issues. Regular inspections and preventive measures can help keep your cedar roof pest-free. Our team at Rhoden Roofing LLC is equipped to address and prevent pest concerns, ensuring the longevity and integrity of your cedar roof.

Myth: Cedar Roofs Aren’t Energy Efficient

Some misconceptions about cedar roofs include the belief that they lack energy-saving benefits. On the contrary, cedar roofs are highly energy efficient. Cedar’s natural insulating properties help regulate indoor temperatures, which can lead to reduced energy consumption for heating and cooling. Additionally, cedar is a renewable and biodegradable resource, making it an environmentally friendly choice. The longevity and minimal environmental impact of cedar further enhance its eco-friendly profile. At Rhoden Roofing LLC, we emphasize the sustainability and energy efficiency of cedar roofing, showcasing its benefits for both homeowners and the environment.

The True Advantages of Cedar Roofs

Clearing up these cedar roof myths reveals the genuine benefits of choosing cedar roofing for your home. Here’s why cedar roofs might be the ideal option:

  1. Aesthetic Appeal: Cedar roofing adds a unique and timeless look to any home. Its natural color variations and texture enhance curb appeal, offering a rustic or traditional appearance that’s hard to match with other materials.
  2. Durability: Cedar shakes and shingles are known for their strength and resilience. Cedar wood naturally resists warping and cracking, and with proper treatment, cedar roofs can withstand harsh weather conditions and last for decades.
  3. Energy Efficiency: Cedar’s insulating properties help maintain comfortable indoor temperatures, reducing the need for heating and cooling. This energy efficiency can lead to lower utility bills and a more comfortable living environment.
  4. Environmental Benefits: Cedar is a renewable and biodegradable material, making it an eco-friendly choice. Its long lifespan and minimal environmental impact contribute to its sustainability.
  5. Value Addition: Installing a cedar roof can increase your home’s value and appeal. Many homebuyers appreciate high-quality, aesthetically pleasing roofs, making cedar a valuable investment.

Rhoden Roofing LLC: Setting the Record Straight on Cedar Roofs

Understanding and addressing cedar roof myths is crucial in making an informed decision about your roofing options. By clarifying these misconceptions and highlighting the true advantages of cedar roofs, we hope to provide you with the knowledge you need. At Rhoden Roofing LLC, we are committed to delivering expert advice and high-quality cedar roofing solutions. If you have questions about cedar roofing or need a consultation, schedule a free estimate with us today to discover the real benefits of cedar roofs for your home.

title.rendered: Protect Your Home: The Importance of Licensed and Insured Roofers in Wichita

content.rendered:
When undertaking roofing projects for your home or business, it’s essential to recognize the significance of engaging licensed and insured roofing professionals. In Wichita, KS, the roofing sector adheres to specific guidelines to guarantee the safety and quality of roofing services. This article will dive into the importance of licensed and insured roofers and their implications for homeowners and business owners in the region.

Why Licensing Matters for Roofers

Licensed roofers in Wichita, KS have met specific standards set by the state or local authorities. These standards ensure that the roofer has the necessary skills, knowledge, and experience to perform roofing work safely and effectively. By hiring a licensed roofer, you can be confident that they have undergone rigorous training and testing, which translates to higher quality work and greater peace of mind for you as a property owner. In addition, roofing contractors in Wichita must comply with local building codes and regulations. Licensed roofers are familiar with these codes and ensure that their work meets or exceeds the required standards. This compliance is particularly important because non-compliance can lead to significant issues, including fines, legal problems, and the potential need for costly rework. Therefore, hiring a licensed roofer ensures that your roofing project is completed according to all applicable laws and regulations.

The Importance of Insurance for Roofers

Hiring insured roofers is just as important as hiring licensed ones. Roofing is a high-risk job; accidents can happen, even with the best roofers. When a roofer is insured, it means they carry liability insurance and workers’ compensation insurance. Liability insurance protects you from financial loss if the roofer causes damage to your property during the project, while workers’ compensation insurance protects you from being held liable if a worker is injured while working on your roof. Imagine hiring a roofer who is not insured. During the project, a worker falls and gets injured. Without insurance, the homeowner could be held responsible for medical bills and other related expenses. This scenario highlights the importance of hiring insured roofers. It protects you from unexpected costs and provides a safety net for both the roofer and yourself.

Identifying the Best Roofers in Wichita, KS

The best roofers in Wichita, KS are not only licensed and insured but also certified by reputable organizations. Certifications from manufacturers or industry bodies indicate that the roofer has received specialized training in specific roofing systems and techniques. This additional expertise ensures that they can handle various roofing materials and complex installations, providing you with the best possible service. Additionally, when searching for the best roofers in Wichita, KS, consider their reputation and customer reviews. A roofer with a solid track record of satisfied customers is more likely to provide high-quality work. Look for reviews on trusted websites and ask for references from the roofer. A reputable roofing contractor will be happy to provide testimonials from past clients.

The Benefits of Hiring Certified Roofers

Certified roofers bring a higher level of expertise and professionalism to your roofing project. Their certification indicates that they have undergone additional training and adhere to industry best practices. This expertise produces better craftsmanship, fewer mistakes, and a longer-lasting roof. Certified roofers are committed to maintaining their reputation and continuously improving their skills, ensuring you receive top-notch service. Additionally, certified roofers often have access to premium materials and products that may not be available to non-certified contractors. This means your roof can benefit from the latest advancements in roofing technology, enhancing its durability, energy efficiency, and aesthetic appeal. Furthermore, manufacturers often provide extended warranties on products installed by certified contractors, giving you added peace of mind. By choosing certified roofers, you’re investing in a higher-quality roofing project with superior materials and long-term benefits.
